question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

Dead men’s shoes

options.text: Making oneself available for all the tasks being assigned
A career where a lot of cheques are signed
Job that one takes over from somebody who has left unexpectedly or died
Acquiring the wealth of a dead man through malpractices

solution:
The correct answer is: **"Job that one takes over from somebody who has left unexpectedly or died."**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Dead men's shoes**" is an idiom that refers to taking over someone's job after they have left or died. (किसी के चले जाने या मर जाने के बाद उसकी नौकरी अपने हाथ में लेना)
 
• The phrase implies that the job is being filled by someone who is not necessarily the most qualified or deserving, but simply because they are available.
 
• The idiom can also suggest a sense of opportunism or taking advantage of a situation.
 
 
• **For example-** *After the CEO unexpectedly resigned, John was able to step into his dead men's shoes and take over the company.*
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: "Making oneself available for all the tasks being assigned." - This option does not relate to the idiom "dead men's shoes."
 
• **Option 2**: "A career where a lot of cheques are signed." - This option does not relate to the idiom "dead men's shoes."
 
• **Option 4**: "Acquiring the wealth of a dead man through malpractices." - This option is not directly related to the idiom "dead men's shoes," but it does involve taking advantage of a situation involving a deceased person.
